title: DR-safe hybrid VPC runtime switchover with live KV reconciliation and automatic rollback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Implement a zero-downtime, disaster-recovery (DR)-aware runtime switchover for Private (VPC) data planes that reconciles live KV state across old and new runtime groups and provides deterministic automatic rollback when health gates fail. This ticket focuses on the orchestration, IaC hooks, safety checks and verification logic needed to perform a hybrid switchover for customers using Dedicated or Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Can perform a phased switchover in a VPC with no 5xx user-visible errors and aggregated p95 tail latency increase < 15%
KV reconciliation completes with <0.01% missing keys and detects divergent writes via transaction checksums
Built-in automatic rollback triggers on any of: traffic-error-rate > 1%, prewarm failure, KV delta > threshold, or tail-latency SLO breach
Terraform module provides explicit lifecycle hooks for preflight, priming, switch, and rollback and can be invoked by customers or the operator
Runbook describes manual remediation steps and how to force-fallback in case of partial reconciliation
End-to-end tests (integration) exercising synthetic traffic, priming, and rollback exist in ci/integration/vpc-switchover-suite
rollout_plan: 1) Preflight: run terraform plan/diff with extra checks (security groups, route tables, version compatibility). 2) Stage group creation: spin up new runtime group in target AZs with feature gates disabled and KV replicas in "read-only shadow" mode. 3) Priming: run controlled synthetic traffic to warm caches (KV prefix priming + embedding cache population) and run read-after-write verifications across a set of golden keys. 4) Reconciliation: perform incremental KV sync with checksum-based verification and record reconciliation report. 5) Canary shift: move 5% traffic to new group, observe metrics (errors, latencies, tail, cpu/gpu utilization). 6) Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health gates at each step. 7) Finalize: promote new group, decommission old group after retention window and sanity checks. 8) Automatic rollback: policy-driven immediate rollback on gated failures, with synthetic failover runs to validate old group health before committing rollback.
health_gates_and_triggers: cpu/gpu throttling or OOM triggers automatic pause and rollback
terraform_integration_notes: Expose lifecycle hooks: preflight_check(), priming_hook(), reconcile_hook(), canary_shift(), finalize_or_rollback(). Provide a 'dry-run' plan output that includes reconciliation estimate and prewarm hit-rate. Make modules idempotent and support 'force-rollback' flag. Add terraform output variables with run IDs and reconciliation artifacts uploaded to s3 for audit.
engineering_tasks: Spec and implement reconciliation algorithm (incremental checksums + tombstone-awareness)
Add priming controller that can replay customer request traces in a privacy-preserving mode
Implement canary traffic router and percent-shift API with immediate rollback capability
Create terraform modules with lifecycle hooks and CI integration
Add observability: per-run reconciliation report, traffic-shift dashboard, and alerting rules
Write integration and chaos tests exercising partial reconciliation and forced rollback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Divergent writes during live migration. Mitigation: enable shadow-writes to both runtimes with compare-by-txid and block final cutover until divergence below threshold.
Risk: Prewarm insufficient causing tail-latency spikes. Mitigation: staged priming using production-like traces and adjustable priming multiplier per model/route.
Risk: Terraform drift during long-running upgrades. Mitigation: lock state during switchover, emit run IDs, support resume-from-step semantics.
Risk: Customer-specific network topologies causing health probe flakiness. Mitigation: provide customer-facing preflight checklist and a proactive synthetic end-to-end probe run as part of preflight
qa_and_testing: CI: integration suite covering canary, rollback, reconciliation under synthetic write patterns. Staging: run against a copy of a customer's tenant slice with telemetry collection. Chaos: inject packet loss, KV write-latency, and process restarts to validate automatic rollback and runbook actions.
security_considerations: Reconciliation artifacts contain hashed keys only; do not store plaintext customer data. Ensure KMS usage for any artifacts in S3 and audit logs exported to the customer workspace. Security review required prior to release.
